changelog: v2.0: Replaced fixed max_feature_missing_ratio with literature-backed tiered strategy per Madley-Dowd 2019, Jakobsen 2017, Sterne 2009
core_principle: Missingness mechanism (MCAR/MAR/MNAR) determines strategy, not proportion alone (Madley-Dowd 2019: 'The proportion of missing data should not be used to guide decisions on multiple imputation')

tier_1_trivial.action: Simple imputation (median for numeric, mode for categorical)
tier_1_trivial.justification: Universally accepted as negligible; complete-case analysis also acceptable (Bennett 2001, Dong & Peng 2013)

tier_2_moderate.action: Multiple imputation (MICE preferred) with mechanism assessment
tier_2_moderate.missing_indicator: required if missingness may be informative (>10%)
tier_2_moderate.justification: Jakobsen 2017: MI reliable in this range under MAR; Sterne 2009: MI preferred over complete-case

tier_3_high.action: MI + missing indicator + mandatory sensitivity analysis (MNAR scenario)
tier_3_high.justification: Madley-Dowd 2019: MI can perform well even at 90% under correct MAR model; Jakobsen 2017 caution applies to MI stability, not to feature retention

tier_4_extreme.action: Per-feature clinical review required. Options: (a) retain as missing indicator only, (b) MI if clinically critical and imputation model well-specified, (c) drop with documented justification
tier_4_extreme.justification: No literature supports automatic exclusion at any threshold. EHR missingness is almost never MCAR (Sperrin 2020). Decision must be per-feature with clinical rationale.

methods: Logistic regression: predict missingness from other observed variables (MAR evidence)
Clinical domain knowledge for MNAR assessment
mechanism_assessment.note: EHR data: assume MAR or MNAR by default. MCAR is rare in clinical data — a missing lab value reflects clinical decision-making.

missing_indicator_policy.evidence_for: Sperrin 2020 (valid for prediction, not causal inference); Groenwold 2012 (CMAJ: valid for prediction); Nijman 2022 (recommends for ML prediction)
missing_indicator_policy.evidence_against: Jones 1996, Knol 2010 (biased for causal inference — does NOT apply to prediction models)
missing_indicator_policy.implementation: Add binary column <feature>_missing before imputation, on each split independently

scale_guard.note: MICE computational cost scales quadratically. For large datasets, use simple imputation + missing indicator as auditable fallback.

reporting_requirements_tripod_ai.item_7a: Report number and proportion missing per variable
reporting_requirements_tripod_ai.item_7d: Report sensitivity analyses for missing data assumptions

literature_references.citation: Madley-Dowd P, Hughes R, Tilling K, Heron J. The proportion of missing data should not be used to guide decisions on multiple imputation. J Clin Epidemiol. 2019;110:63-73.
literature_references.key_finding: Bias depends on mechanism, not proportion. MI works well even at 90% missing under correct MAR model.

literature_references.citation: Jakobsen JC, Gluud C, Wetterslev J, Winkel P. When and how should multiple imputation be used for handling missing data in randomised clinical trials. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2017;17:162.
literature_references.key_finding: 40% threshold for MI stability in RCTs. Does NOT apply to feature selection in prediction models.

literature_references.citation: Sterne JAC, White IR, Carlin JB, et al. Multiple imputation for missing data in epidemiological and clinical research: potential and pitfalls. BMJ. 2009;338:b2393.
literature_references.key_finding: No fixed threshold endorsed. Decision based on mechanism, not proportion.

literature_references.citation: Sperrin M, Martin GP, et al. Missing data should be handled differently for prediction than for description or causal inference. J Clin Epidemiol. 2020;125:183-187.
literature_references.key_finding: Missing indicator method is legitimate for prediction models.

literature_references.citation: Groenwold RHH, et al. Missing covariate data in clinical research: when and when not to use the missing-indicator method for analysis. CMAJ. 2012;184(11):1265-1269.
literature_references.key_finding: Missing indicator valid for prediction, invalid for causal inference.

literature_references.citation: Nijman SWJ, et al. Missing data is poorly handled and reported in prediction model studies using machine learning. J Clin Epidemiol. 2022;142:218-229.
literature_references.key_finding: Most ML studies use ad hoc deletion thresholds without justification. Recommends missing indicators.

literature_references.citation: van Buuren S. Flexible Imputation of Missing Data. 2nd ed. Chapman & Hall/CRC; 2018.
literature_references.key_finding: No fixed threshold for MI failure. Predictive mean matching robust to high missingness.

literature_references.citation: Bennett DA. How can I deal with missing data in my study? Aust N Z J Public Health. 2001;25(5):464-469.
literature_references.key_finding: >10% missingness can bias complete-case analysis, but threshold is for CCA validity, not feature exclusion.

literature_references.citation: Dong Y, Peng CYJ. Principled missing data methods for researchers. SpringerPlus. 2013;2:222.
literature_references.key_finding: Warns against relying on any single threshold. Method choice driven by mechanism.
